title: Rope by Gordon Greenberg at The New Group #ropeplay #thenewgroup #liz...
transcript: Evil gays in New York have always been a dime a dozen, but at least back in the day, they had more that they were up against. In this newly queerified version of the Patrick Hamilton play, Nate and Garrett are hosting a party where dinner is served on a chest housing their murder victim. The period dialogue moves well enough, though the actual plot development feels pretty sluggish. Still, it is interesting to take this story largely about arrogance and power, and apply a queer lens to it. It opens up an exploration of toxic queer relationship dynamics and throws homophobia into the salty cocktail of forces influencing our central characters. Despite the intriguing premise, I struggled to get into this, mostly because I found the characters to be somewhere along the spectrum of irritating to utterly despicable, except for Leila, played by the humorously dry but underused Liz Gillies. Ultimately, what has stuck with me the most from this production is the overwhelming smell of cigarette smoke.
classificationReason: First-hand review of The New Group's queerified Rope with opinions on plot pacing, characters, the queer lens applied to the material, and Liz Gillies' performance; clearly attended
